questions.question_text: Which of these numbers is a perfect square?

options.why: The index of $7$ is odd, so one factor of $7$ is left without a partner and the number is not a perfect square.
The index of $2$ is odd, so one factor of $2$ is left without a partner and the number is not a perfect square.
Both indices are odd, so neither prime can be split into equal pairs.

questions.solution_text:
A number is a perfect square exactly when every index is even.
$2^{4}\times 7^{2}$ has indices $4$ and $2$, both even.
$\sqrt{2^{4}\times 7^{2}}=2^{2}\times 7=28$

questions.question_text: What is the smallest whole number that $2^{2}\times 3^{5}$ must be multiplied by to give a perfect square?

options.why: Assumed the factor $2$ needed pairing, but the index $2$ is already even.
Multiplied by one of each prime instead of only the prime with an odd index.
Added a whole extra pair of $3$s rather than the single unpaired $3$.

questions.solution_text:
Every index must be made even.
The index of $2$ is $2$, which is already even.
The index of $3$ is $5$, so one more $3$ is needed.
$2^{2}\times 3^{5}\times 3=2^{2}\times 3^{6}$
The smallest multiplier is $3$.
